llm.summary: The skill's instructions are broadly consistent with an SDK that sends files to a cloud service, but registry metadata omits the declared install and API-key requirement and the runtime instructions encourage using absolute local file paths — a combination that could enable unexpected data exfiltration if misused.

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md describes an Any-to-Any cloud SDK that legitimately needs a CELLCOG_API_KEY and a client library (pip: cellcog). However, the registry metadata for this skill claims no required env vars, no install, and no required binaries — which contradicts the SKILL.md. The claimed purpose (multi-modal cloud processing) would reasonably require an API key and an SDK, so the omission in the registry appears to be an engineering/inventory inconsistency.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The instructions explicitly show embedding absolute local file paths inside <SHOW_FILE> tags (e.g., /data/...). That model encourages the agent to reference and send arbitrary local files to the remote CellCog service. While this is consistent with a cloud file-processing service, it also creates an obvious avenue for accidental or malicious exfiltration of sensitive local files if the agent is given broad discretion or if users follow example prompts carelessly.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md recommends pip: cellcog as the install step (no version pinned). Registry metadata reported no install spec; this mismatch should be resolved. Installing from PyPI is a common pattern and expected for an SDK, but lack of a pinned version and absence of provenance/homepage in the registry increases risk — you should inspect the package (source, maintainers, release history) before installing.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md requires CELLCOG_API_KEY (recommended via env var). That single credential is proportionate to the described cloud API. However, the registry advertised no required env vars; this inconsistency is concerning. Also, an API key with broad upload/processing rights combined with the ability to reference arbitrary local files raises the impact of accidental credential misuse or data leakage.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No special persistence flags (always, disableModelInvocation) are set in the registry, so the agent could invoke the skill by default. Because the skill sends data to a remote service (and the SKILL.md encourages including absolute file paths), model-invokable behavior increases the risk that the model could autonomously send files to the cloud. The skill does not set disableModelInvocation: true or otherwise limit autonomous invocation — consider this a privilege concern.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to be an SDK for a cloud 'any-to-any' processing service and thus reasonably needs an API key and a Python package — but the registry metadata omits those requirements. Before installing or enabling it: 1) Verify the package and vendor (inspect the pip package source, authors, and PyPI page; prefer installing in an isolated environment). 2) Restrict the CELLCOG_API_KEY scope and use a test account or minimal-permission key. 3) Avoid giving the agent blanket permission to read or send arbitrary local files; do not include sensitive file paths in prompts. 4) Prefer requiring explicit user invocation (or set disableModelInvocation) so the model cannot autonomously upload files. 5) Ask the publisher/registry owner to fix the metadata discrepancies (install spec and required env) and to provide an official homepage and privacy/security documentation.
